channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Eleições 2026: acompanhe a disputa entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro no 2º turno e a votação no Brasil e no exterior
item.description: Polls are open from 8am to 5pm this Sunday, October 25, for the runoff election between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro. BBC News Brasil will provide live coverage with vote counting starting at 4:30pm.

item.title: Trump tem que ficar de fora da política do Brasil, diz New York Times
item.description: The New York Times published an editorial stating that President Donald Trump should stay out of Brazil's politics during the presidential election runoff. The publication emphasized the importance of national autonomy in elections.

item.title: Haddad vota em SP e destaca 'clima excelente' nas ruas
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) voted in São Paulo and highlighted an 'excellent atmosphere' on the streets, emphasizing Lula's legacy for the runoff election. Defeated for São Paulo governor, he stressed the continuation of progressive policies.

item.title: Lula chega para votar em São Bernardo (SP)
item.description: Lula arrived at the polling station in São Bernardo do Campo, SP, to cast his vote in the 2026 municipal election, emphasizing his commitment to civic participation.

item.title: Segundo turno: eleitores poderão enfrentar temporal e ventos de até 100 km/hora, alerta INMET
item.description: The 2026 runoff election takes place this Sunday, with voters choosing between Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) for president, and in some states, governor. The INMET warns of adverse weather conditions including winds up to 100 km/h and heavy rains that may impact the electoral process.

item.title: Eventual vitória de Flávio consolidaria 'onda azul' da direita, diz jornal La Nación
item.description: Argentine newspaper La Nación claims that a victory by Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the 2026 Brazilian presidential election would consolidate a 'blue wave' of right-wing governments in Latin America. The article highlights the growing influence of conservative leaders in the region.

item.title: Eleições 2026: brasileiros reclamam de filas para votar no exterior
item.description: Brazilian voters abroad face long lines and logistical challenges while casting ballots in the 2026 elections, particularly in cities like Paris, Lisbon, and Dublin. Voting began in New Zealand and now spans 134 countries, with approximately 918,876 eligible voters. Overseas Brazilians can only vote for president and vice-president.

item.title: Famosos votam no 2º turno das eleições de 2026; FOTOS
item.description: Citizens and public figures visited the polls in the 2026 runoff election, contested between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Voting takes place nationwide, with gubernatorial races in five states. Entertainment personalities were spotted at their respective polling stations.

item.title: Antes de votar, Lula agradece eleitores e alfineta Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: President Lula thanked voters for their support and cast his ballot in São Bernardo do Campo. Before voting, he criticized Flávio Bolsonaro, calling him a liar and saying the people won't elect a liar. Lula received 45% of valid votes in the first round, behind Flávio.

item.title: Guia das Eleições 2026: ônibus e metrô de graça para votar e tudo o que você precisa saber no 2º turno
item.description: In the 2026 runoff election, public transportation (buses, metro, trains, ferries) will be free nationwide per a Supreme Court ruling. Voting takes place Sunday, October 25, from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. (Brasília time), with each city managing the free service schedule. Cutting transport on election day is an electoral offense.

item.title: Cantora lamenta não poder votar e recebe o carinho da torcida lulista
item.description: Singer Marina Sena publicly regretted being unable to vote in the 2026 runoff election, despite having campaigned for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). Her statement sparked mixed reactions, including criticism from Lula supporters for not exercising her right to vote. The post gained significant attention on social media, drawing responses from both supporters and opponents.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro vence Lula no Japão no 2º turno das eleições
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) defeated Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) in Japan during the second round of the 2026 presidential elections, securing 80.08% of the valid votes. The election was held earlier due to the time zone difference, allowing Brazilian residents to vote before polls opened in Brazil. Japan ranks as the third-largest electoral college for Brazilians abroad.

item.title: Moraes vota e diz que sistema eleitoral do Brasil é o melhor do mundo
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes voted and praised the Brazilian electoral system as the best in the world. PoderData poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva tied in the second round, with 51% and 49% of valid votes respectively.

item.title: Restaurante fecha no 2º turno após denúncia de impedir equipe de votar
item.description: The Estrela do Sul restaurant in Brasília's North Wing decided to close on Election Day following allegations of preventing employees from voting in the first round. The Labor Public Ministry intervened to ensure workers' voting rights, recommending flexible work schedules. Management stated the closure aims to prevent voting difficulties while respecting employees' freedom of conscience.

item.title: Lula chega a colégio em São Bernardo do Campo para votar no 2º turno
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) voted in the second round of the 2026 elections in São Bernardo do Campo, accompanied by his wife Janja, Vice President Geraldo Alckmin, and former minister Fernando Haddad. After voting, Lula went to his hotel on Paulista Avenue to follow the vote count, facing a disadvantage in São Paulo state against Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Davi Alcolumbre vota no Amapá e faz chamado à paz e ao respeito
item.description: The President of the Senate, Davi Alcolumbre, voted in Macapá (AP) and emphasized the importance of freedom of choice, peace, and respect on election day. After voting, he headed to Brasília and, at noon, will visit the TSE alongside the President of the Chamber, Hugo Motta.

item.title: Pesquisas eleitorais mostram a distância entre Flávio e Lula após últimos números da semana
item.description: Recent polls show a technical tie between Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) for the runoff, with variations between surveys. The gap between candidates ranges from 0.2 percentage points (Futura) to four points (Gerp), keeping the race balanced.

item.title: Como saber se seu local de votação mudou no 2º turno
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court advises voters to confirm their polling place before the second round, as addresses may change. The data is updated four times daily and can vary until Sunday, so it is important to use only official channels.

item.title: Votos do Nordeste demoram mais para chegar ao TSE? Tudo para acompanhar a apuração
item.description: Votes from the Northeast and North take longer to be counted by the TSE, affecting the electoral vote count. In 2014, this delay nearly favored Aécio Neves before Dilma Rousseff reversed the outcome.

item.title: Derrite vota e cita redução da maioridade penal como prioridade
item.description: Elected senator Guilherme Derrite (PP-SP) voted in São Paulo and emphasized the reduction of the criminal age of majority as a congressional priority in 2027, reaffirming his support for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the presidential race and projecting a widening vote margin in the second round.

item.title: Elecciones en Brasil, en vivo | Casi 160 millones de brasileños definen el futuro del país entre Lula y Bolsonaro
item.description: Around 160 million Brazilian voters are set to decide the next president in a runoff between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and ultrarightist Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro convicted of attempting a coup. Flávio, who voted early in Rio de Janeiro, emphasized calls for change, stating Brazil can no longer endure the status quo.

item.title: Eleição começa com chuva e vento em Berlim; Joanna Maranhão se emociona ao falar de Lula
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian elections continue with the runoff vote in Berlin, where citizens cast their ballots under rain and 8°C cold. Joanna Maranhão, presidential candidate, becomes emotional when speaking about Lula, as shorter lines form outside the Brazilian Embassy. Adverse weather and emotional speeches underscore the tense electoral atmosphere in this decisive phase.

item.title: TSE agiliza aprovação de transporte para indígenas e quilombolas
item.description: The TSE, led by Minister Kassio Nunes Marques, approved a streamlined procedure to authorize transportation for indigenous, quilombola and traditional community voters to polling stations in the second round, replacing per-trip analysis with joint authorizations previously planned by the Union. The measure maintains the requirement for judicial authorization and prohibits political campaigning during transfers, aiming to ensure access and speed in electoral logistics.

item.title: Lula ataca Flávio: “Ele tem uma preferência por mentir”
item.description: Lula (PT) labeled Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) a liar during the second-round voting, praising the campaign and the unprecedented popular mobilization. The president described his opponent as 'a citizen called Lie,' reinforcing criticisms of the PL's messaging.

item.title: Kassio Nunes vota em Brasília e diz esperar eleição tranquila
item.description: TSE president Minister Kassio Nunes Marques voted in Brasília and expects a peaceful election. PoderData poll shows a technical tie between Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula in the second round.

item.title: Lula destaca mobilização popular e Flávio Bolsonaro defende mudança; candidatos votam pela manhã
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro cast their votes in the 2026 election runoff. Lula highlighted an unprecedented popular mobilization during the campaign, while Flávio called for change in the country, criticizing insecurity and the worsening quality of life. Both emphasized the importance of voter turnout.

item.title: Vídeo: Vai votar no 2º turno? Confira os documentos obrigatórios e dicas do TSE
item.description: The video provides TSE guidance on the required documents and procedures for voting in the runoff, including the need to bring an ID and a 'cheat sheet' with candidate information. The Chief Electoral Management Advisor, Sandra Damiani, emphasizes the importance of following electronic voting rules and avoiding errors in the process.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro x Lula após Datafolha e Quaest: o que mostra o Agregador de Pesquisas da BBC?
item.description: The BBC Polling Data aggregator shows Flávio Bolsonaro leading with 48% against Lula's 46% in the 2026 second-round election, with 6% for 'no candidate'. In valid votes, the split remains 50.8% for Bolsonaro and 49.2% for Lula.

item.title: Brasil escolhe hoje entre o retorno de um Bolsonaro e o 4º mandato de Lula
item.description: Over 158 million eligible Brazilian voters choose today between the return of Jair Bolsonaro to power and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's government continuing for another four years. The 2026 election unfolds amid national polarization, with key debates centered on economy, security, and corruption. The campaign was marked by mutual criticism and promises of structural reforms.

item.title: Lula x Flávio nas novas pesquisas de segundo turno: veja números atualizados
item.description: Six institutes released polls for the runoff election between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), with tight margins. The race remains competitive between the two candidates.

item.title: Datafolha, Quaest, Palver, BTG/Nexus, Atlas: veja últimas pesquisas do segundo turno
item.description: Datafolha, Quaest, Palver, BTG/Nexus and AtlasIntel/Bloomberg polls measure the 2026 Brazilian presidential runoff between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) with margins of error ranging from 1 to 2.2 points.

item.title: Um herdeiro de clã em constante provação: Flávio Bolsonaro supera desconfiança sob o desafio de aplacar divisões
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro confirmed his presidential candidacy during a meeting at the traditional A Bela Sintra restaurant in São Paulo. As a clan heir under constant scrutiny, he faces the challenge of overcoming distrust and bridging divisions within his political base.

item.title: Zebras fora do radar: pesquisas indicam chances baixas de viradas nos estados com segundo turno
item.description: Surveys released before the second round of state elections show low chances of upsets, with candidates leading in the first round maintaining their advantages. Flávio Bolsonaro and Celina Leão lead in their respective races, while Omar Aziz and Lorenzo Pazolini also hold wide margins over opponents.

item.title: Por que Flávio Bolsonaro? Segurança, economia e rejeição ao PT dão o tom entre eleitores do senador
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro leads polling with proposals on security, economy and anti-PT rhetoric, backed by voters who reject Lula and value family, religion and the legacy of his father Jair.

item.title: Máquina garante voto? Tempo de TV muda tudo? A polarização cansou? As máximas eleitorais colocadas em xeque em 2026
item.description: The 2026 electoral results challenged traditional assumptions, such as the influence of the public machine, party alliances, and polarization fatigue. Personalist candidates and targeted campaigns won over broader coalitions, questioning long-held beliefs about alliances and TV exposure. The election also highlighted the use of AI for misinformation and voter volatility.

item.title: Ajuste fiscal, juros, produtividade, IA: a longa lista de desafios econômicos no horizonte do próximo presidente
item.description: The economy will be a central challenge for the next president, regardless of whether Lula or Flávio Bolsonaro wins. The victor will need to address financial sector pressure for fiscal adjustments and a challenging macroeconomic environment both domestically and internationally.

item.title: Com 51% a 49% no Datafolha e na Quaest, Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula chegam à eleição com a menor diferença em 20 anos
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are in a technical tie in polls, marking the smallest electoral gap in 20 years. The pro-Lula wave did not consolidate, and polling projections favor Flávio. Lula's administration has finally surpassed disapproval rates.

item.title: Lulinha, Supremo, 'Dark horse': a cronologia da corrida presidencial em oito pontos
item.description: The 2026 election race between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) concluded after a campaign marked by a crisis at the STF and the 'Dark Horse' scandal. Lula leads among the poorest (58%) and Flávio, among the wealthy (57%), according to Quaest.

item.title: A última dança por uma virada inédita: surpreendido no primeiro turno, Lula ressurge aprendendo com as ruas e as redes
item.description: In the 1982 election, Lula was polling third place on the eve of his bid for São Paulo governor, despite captivating crowds and performing well in TV debates. The article captures his exhaustion and confidence ahead of an unexpected outcome.

item.title: Seja Flávio ou Lula: do Supremo ao Congresso, presidente eleito terá de lidar com tensão elevada entre Poderes
item.description: The 2026 election between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro will intensify tensions among the Powers, with distinct governance strategies. Lula seeks to reorganize his base and negotiate with Centrão, while Flávio relies on parliamentary majority and pressure on the STF. Both face challenges in implementing their agendas amid polarization and institutional conflicts.

item.title: Eleição histórica que chega ao fim hoje dará poder inédito a uma única família ou terá a primeira virada já registrada
item.description: The tenth presidential election since the return to democracy is decided today between Flávio Bolsonaro and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. If Flávio wins, three members of the Bolsonaro family will hold simultaneous offices in Congress. If Lula wins, it will mark the first historical comeback after trailing in the first round.

item.title: Após peso inédito na campanha, política externa colocará o novo presidente entre o pragmatismo e a afinidade ideológica
item.description: Foreign policy has become a central theme in the 2026 presidential race, driven by Donald Trump's tariffs and U.S. interference supporting Flávio Bolsonaro. The contest between Lula and the far-right involves balancing pragmatism and ideological alignment amid tariff pressures and calls for Jair Bolsonaro's pardon.

item.title: Por que Lula? Proteção social, meio ambiente e soberania norteiam eleitores do petista
item.description: Lula's voters highlight social protection, environmental defense, and sovereignty as voting reasons, recalling programs like Bolsa Família and SUS strengthening. The campaign emphasizes environmental preservation and national sovereignty against foreign interests. For some, the vote reflects more rejection of the Bolsonaro family than support for the government.

item.title: Sob a missão dos generais: como canais do WhatsApp mobilizaram os eleitores de Flávio e Lula no segundo turno
item.description: WhatsApp channels like 'Exército do Lula' and 'Tropa do Flávio' mobilized voters in the runoff, shaping the digital strategy of the campaigns. The PT channel reached 10.8 million followers, while the PL channel had 2.1 million, underscoring the role of social media in guiding grassroots activism and voter engagement.

item.title: Posso ir votar de bermuda? Veja o que é proibido nas eleições
item.description: In the 2026 elections, there is no legal prohibition on clothing for voting, but beachwear such as bikinis or thongs should be avoided by common sense. It is allowed to show personal preference with flags or brooches, but it is prohibited to promote gatherings, carry out collective propaganda, or bring phones and devices inside the voting booth. Practices such as approaching voters, distributing gifts, or carrying weapons are also forbidden, subject to penalties.

item.title: Pesquisa PoderData/Aya: leia os resultados de Lula e Flávio no 2º turno
item.description: A PoderData/Aya survey released on October 25, 2026 shows a technical tie between Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) with 51% and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) with 49% of valid votes in the second round. Both voting intentions match the previous survey from October 22, with a margin of error of 1.6 percentage points.

item.title: Mulheres e pardos: o perfil dos 2,2 milhões de eleitores do DF no 2º turno
item.description: In the 2026 second-round elections in the Federal District, 2,253,732 eligible voters will participate, with female (54%) and brown (49.17%) majorities. Approximately 426,000 voters abstained in the first round, and 273,434 voter registrations are canceled. Key races include Celina Leão vs. Leandro Grass for governor and Lula vs. Flávio Bolsonaro for president.

item.title: Lula vence Flávio na Nova Zelândia; acompanhe votação no exterior
item.description: In the 2026 overseas elections, 918,876 Brazilians voted. In the first round, Lula won 64 countries and Flávio 37, but Flávio led with 47.03% against Lula's 45.16%. In New Zealand, Lula secured 80.54% in the second round.

item.title: Saiba como estão Lula e Flávio nas últimas 18 pesquisas divulgadas
item.description: The 18 most recent national polls for the 2026 runoff show Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) ahead of President Lula da Silva (PT) in 17 of them, with 1 tie and none indicating a win for Lula. The polls, conducted between October 12 and 24, consider only valid votes, excluding blanks, nulls, and undecideds.

item.title: Trunfo de Lula, jovens são os que menos pretendem votar no 2º turno
item.description: A survey conducted by DataFolha on October 23-24, 2026 shows that young people aged 16 to 24 are the least likely to confirm their intention to vote in the presidential runoff. Although Lula leads with 53% against 42% in this age group, lower turnout intentions may hinder translating this support into actual votes. Older voters show higher voting likelihood and lean toward Flávio Bolsonaro.
